newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala names commission to oversee peace.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala names commission to oversee peace.

text.p: The Guatemalan government and ex-guerrillas set up a joint commission on Wednesday to oversee the implementation of December peace accords that ended 36 years of war.

"All the actors that contributed to the successful peace negotiation and now must contribute to the success of a new phase in constructing peace are represented on this commission," Jean Arnault, the United Nations moderator during the peace talks, told a news conference.
Citizen representatives, government officials and former rebels of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) sit on the commission.
It was formed as aspects of the historic peace accord signed on Dec. 29 ending Latin America's longest and last guerrilla war, have begun stirring controversy.

Hundreds of military police rebelled for several days over aspects of the peace accords last week, but surrendered on Sunday after the army threatened them with heavy artillery. The police were demanding severance pay when their unit is cut under terms of the accord.
Under the peace agreement the army will be cut by one third, which is also causing confusion.
In November, the army pledged to make cuts across the ranks but this week army officials said cuts would only affect the military police and enlisted men.

"(The accords) must be understood to mean that officers as well as troops are reduced. Thse are things that this commission will have to look at," said Jorge Soto, formerly known as commander Pablo Monsanto, one of the URNG representatives on the commission.
